body:
Found while stress-testing the Inspector with huge collections.

**What happens.** A page with 1,200 collection items produces one 73s long task, even without the Inspector mounted. At 150 rows the same task takes about 2s, so the cost grows faster than the item count. With the Inspector mounted it's worse.

**Where.** The CPU profile puts it in the runtime's bundled Playwright selector evaluator, `_queryCSS` (seen in `packages/ayme/dist/runtime-*.mjs`). Every query concatenates arrays and walks `querySelectorAll` again, so resolving many items' locators repeats the same traversal.

This is a runtime problem rather than an Inspector one, and likely needs the locator resolution for a collection batched or cached.

comments.body:
The same cost shows up on every agent call through `ayme mcp`, at a few hundred rows. Measured in the 2026-10-28 dogfood run on main `d75498f` (headless Chromium, example-vue dev server). Fixture: the bench Projects page, each `li` a `ProjectRow` (rooted, one Locator member, three actions), rows from `page.getByRole("list", { name: "Projects" }).locator(":scope > li")`, plus a button that appends 50 rows.

`hover` on a static heading (ms):

| Rows | Role locator | CSS locator (`ul[aria-label="Projects"] > li`) | No Page Objects | Role locator, Inspector off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 439 | 422 | 387 | 415 |
| 55 | 1402 | 617 | 424 | 1141 |
| 105 | 2861 | 1166 | 483 | 2584 |
| 155 | 5197 | 2116 | 535 | 5609 |
| 306 | 18492 | | | |

- `snapshot` at 155 rows: 1.15 s with the role locator, 0.35 s with CSS, 54 ms with no Page Objects. At 306 rows it is 4.3 s.
- At 306 rows, page-side Page Object actions time out at their 1 s locator timeout (`ProjectRow.moveUp` → `TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 1000ms exceeded`). A `reload` takes 10 s.
- A CPU profile of one 21 s hover at 306 rows: `observePomRoot` 12.8 s inclusive, `resolveAll` 10.7 s, `walkMembers` 6.5 s, `count` 6.4 s, `isVisible` 3.2 s, `measurePomRoot` 3.6 s. Nearly all self time is in the selector engine (`queryAll`, `query`, `getAriaRole`, `querySelectorAll`). The ARIA capture itself is 0.27 s.
- **Not a regression:** a build of `7f1b9279` (before #1046 to #1056, with the same playwright-lite dist) gives the same curve: 420 / 1231 / 2838 / 6149 ms.

The role locator costs about 2.5 times the CSS one, but both grow faster than the row count. A plain list of the same size stays near 0.5 s (#846's sub-issues cover that part).

## Triage Notes

Category: `bug`. State: `needs-triage`, approved by Abel.

**What is established:**
- The Oct 28 comment supplies stronger current-main evidence than the original report: growing role/CSS collection costs, a near-flat no-Page-Objects baseline, CPU profiles dominated by selector work, and comparison against the older build. It reports this is not a regression from the recent fixes.
- Some caching already exists: resolveTargets resolves the same Locator object once per pass. That does not establish that the whole collection observation is bounded: root observation, member count(), visibility and other reads still perform their own work. Searches covered the Page Object walk, resolveTargets, the Lite page driver/root observation, and related large-page issues. No complete fix for the reported curve was found.
- This pass inspected code and the recorded measurements; it did not rerun the stress fixture or independently reproduce the reported 73-second task. No `.out-of-scope/` rejection records exist.

**Next triage work:**
Reduce the captured stress fixture to a repeatable reproduction and attribute repeated selector work to Ayme's call pattern versus Playwright Lite behavior. Preserve the same Page Objects and observable results while comparing the paths. Follow the repository's fork rule: any behavior where Lite differs from Playwright is fixed upstream; an Ayme-specific reduction of repeated reads belongs in Ayme. Do not assume a cross-call cache is safe on a changing page.

Keep this separate from the plain large-page costs in #846 "On a page with thousands of elements every call takes 5 to 15 seconds and snapshots run to 500+ KB" and the Inspector-only hit-test invalidation in #1020 "Selecting a structure node on a busy page stalls it, as each hit test restyles the whole Inspector". Once attribution and the intended bounded work are clear, write an agent brief with a deterministic work-count check plus measured timings.
